record_type_quote: This study sought to conceptually replicate and extend Barrett et al.’s (2010) pioneering work exploring music-evoked nostalgia, where the authors identiﬁed person- and context-level predictors of the experience of nostalgia in music.

targets.authors: Barrett, F. S., Grimm, K. J., Robins, R. W., Wildschut, T., Sedikides, C., & Janata, P.
targets.title: Music-evoked nostalgia: Affect, memory, and personality.
targets.evidence_quote: This study sought to conceptually replicate and extend Barrett et al.’s (2010) pioneering work exploring music-evoked nostalgia, where the authors identiﬁed person- and context-level predictors of the experience of nostalgia in music.
targets.outcome_quote: Overall, the results of the present study are largely consistent with Barrett et al. (2010), conceptually replicating the ﬁndings in a larger and more diverse sample.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly summarize the results overall as largely consistent and conceptually replicating the findings. Under rule 1 this overall verdict takes precedence over specific discrepancies: negative valence and the BANPS play/PANAS negative-affect predictors did not replicate. The conclusion also describes the majority of findings as replicated.

reasoning: A new sample and personalized music retest the 2010 empirical paper. The 2013 Barrett paper supplies the personality measure and is not a target.
